rationale: The candidate reads as a compact but over-compacted split/stacked bar that is only partly coherent across views. The top view suggests a fractured, rotationally confused mass with a void-like center, while the elevations show a stepped, blocky object rather than one dominant inhabitable gesture. The road frontage edge is not convincingly activated: there is no clear public threshold, court, undercut, or seam aligned to the verified access edge, so the ground response feels sealed rather than inviting. The stepped language is present but not legible as a capacity-bearing inhabited section; it reads more like arbitrary tiering than a programmatic terrace or roof logic. Because the building type is neighborhood living, the form needs a stronger ground/public relation and a calmer, more continuous upper hierarchy. The current mass can be repaired into a better bar/court hybrid, but as shown it does not hard-pass program fit.
